title: Capstone: The Launch Review
objective: After this lesson you will be able to assemble a launch evidence bundle (scores, gates, budgets, guardrails, runbooks, residual risks), present it for approval, and operate the shipped agent with the dashboards and rituals this course built.
why: Courses end with artifacts that survive stakeholders: the launch bundle proves readiness with evidence, names residual risks with owners, and hands operations a running system with dashboards, runbooks, and rituals. This walkthrough performs the review once — your capstone repeats it on your own agent, and your career repeats it on every launch after.

blocks.text: Five sections, all evidenced: (1) **Gap closure** — audit re-run, every dimension owned with proof links; (2) **Budgets** — latency/cost models from measurements with headroom; (3) **Safety** — fallback chaos results, guardrail attack-gold scores, gate/canary/rollback proof; (4) **Operations** — dashboards live, alerts firing-correctly (tested), review queue staffed, runbooks practiced; (5) **Residual risks** — what remains, with owners and dates (no silent hope).

blocks.caption: Manifest-first launch: every claim has proof attached or an owner dated

blocks.text: Present weakest-first (residual risks open, not buried): scores per segment with the weakest named, one iterated fix with delta, gate health, chaos results, then the ask (launch scope + rollback plan). Approval is conditional by default (launch to 10% with canary armed) — full traffic follows measured canary, never meeting optimism.

Operating cadence post-launch: weekly gold re-scores with per-segment review, monthly cost/latency budget reviews, quarterly chaos + gate audits, per-release gap re-audits. Rituals compound: each cycle's findings become next cycle's gold items, gates, and guardrails. Launched systems improve monotonically or decay silently — rituals choose.

blocks.title: Audit the bundle
blocks.note: Run it: expect five PASS lines then conditional approval. Residual risks with owners/dates pass review; silent hopes block it — the bundle proves readiness, the residuals prove honesty.

items: Bundle: gap closure + budgets + safety proof + ops readiness + owned residual risks
Present weakest-first; approve conditionally (canary-gated %) by default
Day-two rituals (weekly/monthly/quarterly/per-release) compound improvements or decay silently

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the bundle audit and confirm conditional approval. (b) Break it (drop attack gold to 10/12) and state the review outcome + required fix. (c) Draft your capstone bundle skeleton (same five sections) with one evidence line per section for your domain.
hints: Baseline: 5 PASS + conditional approval (residuals owned, not absent).
Broken: attack-gold check FAILs → launch BLOCKED until 12/12 (gates gate launches, not just merges).
Your skeleton needs per-section evidence lines (scores, margins, proofs, staffing, owned residuals) — coverage thinking for launches.
exercise.why: Break-then-block practices gate enforcement at launch scale: missing proof blocks shipping, with the exact fix named. Coverage thinking extends from code to launches.
exercise.code: // Launch-audit pattern: per-section evidence checks + owned-residual rule.

quiz.q: Launch bundle shows green averages, one weak segment unnamed. Verdict?
options: Block until weakest named with fix-or-accept decision: unnamed weak segments hide localized harm
quiz.explain: Weakest-first presentation is the honesty rule: per-segment truth with named handling beats green averages that conceal.

quiz.q: Approve full traffic at the review meeting?
options: Conditionally (canary-gated %) with measured promotion after — full traffic follows canary evidence, never meeting optimism
quiz.explain: Conditional approval is the default: canary percentages with vetoes armed, promotion on measured green. Meetings decide scope; canaries decide scale.

options: Rituals: weekly re-scores, monthly budgets, quarterly chaos/audits, per-release gap audits — findings become gold/gates/guardrails cyclically
quiz.explain: Monotonic improvement is ritual-driven: each cycle's findings feed the next cycle's prevention. Hope is not a system.

summary: Evidence bundles, weakest-first reviews, conditional canary approvals, day-two rituals. Launches approved on proof with owned residuals — then operated into monotonic improvement.
